title: A Controlled Audit of Personal AI Memory for Rating Prediction
question: Does a memory system preserve the information a decision actually needs?
summary: I compare full histories and extracted memories, then shuffle within-user associations to separate useful structure from superficial signals. On the Coat task, extracted memory increased prediction error for both tested LLM readers.
boundary: A controlled rating-prediction study. MovieLens effects were small and inconclusive after adjustment; this is not a claim about every use of AI memory.

title: Exact Memory-Time Optimization for Prefix-Cached Language Model Serving
question: What is a cached block worth if its required prefix has already disappeared?
summary: I formulate prefix-aware retention as a maximum-weight closure problem solved by a minimum cut. The result accounts for dependencies that independent block optimization misses, with an exact extension beyond a fixed timeout grid.
boundary: Experiments measure usable prefix blocks and storage time, not GPU latency. A finer training optimum did not consistently improve held-out performance.

title: Verification Pulses and the Cost of Escaping Wrong Consensus
question: When is correcting an answer enough to stop a wrong consensus spreading?
summary: I study how the timing and targeting of a limited verification budget affect recovery. Exact finite-population calculations distinguish crossing an average threshold from achieving a high probability of eventual correction.
boundary: Results apply to a specified update model. All four adjusted schedule-comparison intervals in the language-model experiment included zero.

title: Contingent Exposure Routing for Financial AI: Outage Risk and the Cost of Indivisible Decisions
question: Can a shared fallback concentrate the very risk it was meant to reduce?
summary: I connect model outages to shared decision errors and study routing choices when decisions cannot be split. Bounds, synthetic networks and a recorded-response replay make the tradeoff between availability and concentration explicit.
boundary: An auditable routing stress test, not a prediction of market crashes. The recorded-response replay uses constructed rebalancing tasks.

title: Marginally Correct Tool Caches Can Reverse Group-Normalized Policy Updates
question: Can individually correct cached results still change what a policy learns?
summary: I show how sharing stochastic tool results can change dependence within a group even when each reward keeps the right marginal distribution. In a controlled model, that dependence can reverse the expected update.
evidence: Exact analysis · exhaustive numerical checks · code audit
boundary: A mathematical and implementation audit. It does not claim a measured reversal in large-language-model training.

title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices
question: Does an agent’s choice reveal what the customer values?
summary: I distinguish executing a delegated task from identifying a worthwhile product improvement. The analysis separates decisions that need more evidence from decisions that cannot be identified from the observed agent choices alone.
boundary: Controlled models and simulations, without human participants or measured customer outcomes.
